title: Symbol namespace isolation with canary validation and adaptive probe tuning
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Background: Our heterogeneous GPU fleet occasionally encounters symbol collisions and ABI mismatches when multiple CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA versions are present on the same image. These surface as cold-start failures, intermittent kernel link errors, and non-deterministic perf regressions on customer workloads. This ticket implements a pragmatic isolation layer (symbol namespace isolation + lazy-link probing) together with a small canary validation harness and adaptive probe tuning to reduce rollout risk and reduce probe latency.
goals: 1) Isolate vendor/shared symbol resolution so multiple CUTLASS/Triton bundles can co-exist and not corrupt the runtime symbol table. 2) Implement an adaptive probe strategy that reduces probe jitter on cold-starts while maintaining correctness. 3) Ship a canary validation job and CI gating that exercises the isolation layer across representative model binaries. 4) Reduce customer-facing kernel load failures by >= 90% and probe latency variance by 50% in canary fleets.
non_goals: Replace the kernel selection engine or rewrite CUTLASS adapters. This work is focused on safe isolation, probing, and validation; deeper kernel dispatch refactors are out of scope.
approach: Phase A: build a lightweight symbol namespace shim implemented with an LD_PRELOAD-compatible loader that creates an isolated symbol domain per bundle and exposes a controlled interop surface (well-defined vtables). Phase B: implement lazy-symbol resolution with an adaptive backoff that uses historical probe success/failure telemetry to skip known-bad bundle paths. Phase C: implement a canary pipeline (nightly + on-deploy) that runs microbenchmarks and integration traces against a matrix of CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS combos. Phase D: roll out to canary pool, collect metrics, iterate on backoff heuristics and fallback policies.
design_decisions: - Chose symbol-namespace shim over full binary re-linking to minimize build changes. - Use LD_PRELOAD because it is OS portable across our fleet and allows us to intercept symbol lookups without altering downstream binaries. - Keep a minimal public API surface between bundles to avoid deep ABI coupling. - Persist probe results and success rates in the existing runtime telemetry store to inform adaptive skip logic.
success_criteria: - Canary fleet shows <1% kernel load failures for tested combos within 72 hours. - Median probe latency reduced by >=25ms and p95 reduced by >=50% versus current baseline. - No customer incidents traceable to symbol collisions after 2-week canary. - CI gates added and green for the full compat matrix.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: LD_PRELOAD behavior differences across distros could cause leaks or inconsistent resolution. Mitigation: add distro-specific unit tests in canary CI and fall back to containerized shim when detection fails. Risk: adaptive skip policy may mask regressions. Mitigation: periodic forced probe (once per 24h) and alerting when telemetry drops below threshold.
